# @edwyn/signature-style — The Signature Style (full)

> Catppuccin Mocha-based design system: Token Cascade, Override Protocol, Chromatic Palette content colors, mechanical physics.

Version: 3.8.0 · Edition: Harmonized — 100% official Catppuccin, per-theme (Mocha dark default / OLED true-black / Daylight high-contrast; Latte light legacy)

GENERATED by playground/generate-llms.mjs (`npm run llms`) from snippets.ts + tokens.json + SYSTEM_PROMPT.md + react/*.d.ts. Regenerate after any source change — never hand-edit.

## The 50-Token Whitelist

### Mocha (dark default — theme tokens; Latte swaps the values by `[data-theme="latte"]`, same names)

- `--bg-base` `#1E1E2E` — Catppuccin Mocha base — page and app background.
- `--bg-surface` `#313244` — Mocha surface0 — cards, inputs, secondary buttons, disabled surfaces.
- `--bg-canvas` `var(--bg-base)` — 3.2.0 ALIAS — the owner's --bg-canvas name resolving to --bg-base in every theme (OLED true black included). Same slot, two names; whitelist 50 → 51.
- `--color-cake-primary` `#F2CDCD` — Catppuccin Mocha Flamingo — primary actions. Official palette color; per-theme harmony means the dark side of the toggle wears Mocha's own accent.
- `--color-cake-secondary` `#94E2D5` — Catppuccin Mocha Teal — focus rings and secondary accents. Official palette color; per-theme harmony means the dark side of the toggle wears Mocha's own accent.
- `--text-main` `#CDD6F4` — Mocha text — primary text.
- `--text-muted` `#7F849C` — Mocha overlay0 — subtitles, hints, disabled labels.
- `--bg-inset` `#282A36` — KEEPER — legacy deep grey. Inset wells, code blocks, input interiors.
- `--text-bright` `#F8F8F2` — KEEPER — legacy off-white. Maximum-contrast emphasis text and headings.
- `--color-success` `#A8E6CF` — KEEPER — legacy soft mint. Success actions.
- `--text-muted-soft` `#6272A4` — KEEPER — legacy dimmed blue. Tertiary text, quiet captions.

### Latte (light opt-in — the same token names, official Latte values)

- `--bg-base` `#EFF1F5`
- `--bg-surface` `#CCD0DA`
- `--color-cake-primary` `#DD7878`
- `--color-cake-secondary` `#179299`
- `--text-main` `#4C4F69`
- `--text-muted` `#6272A4`
- `--bg-inset` `#E6E9EF`
- `--text-bright` `#11111B`
- `--color-success` `#A8E6CF`
- `--text-muted-soft` `#8C8FA1`

### Shared (theme-independent, defined once in :root)

- `--color-on-cake` `#1E1E2E` — Text/icon color placed on top of cake-colored surfaces. Same value in both themes.
- `--font-sans` `"Inter", system-ui, sans-serif` — Global default font: Inter (weights 400 text / 500 buttons / 600 headings), system-ui fallback offline.
- `--radius-ui` `6px` — Minimalist corners for every interactive surface.
- `--radius-card` `12px` — 3.0.0 — card corners: cards earn rounder corners than 6px controls. Owner references var(--radius-card) on the archetype surfaces.
- `--transition-standard` `all 0.15s ease-out` — Mechanical motion for colors and opacity — snappy, no bounce.
- `--transition-transform` `transform 0.3s cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.8, 0.2, 1)` — Motion for transforms (press scale, lifts) — smooth arrival, no bounce.
- `--space-tight` `0.5rem` — 8px grid tier 1 — tight gaps, vertical button padding.
- `--space-standard` `1rem` — 8px grid tier 2 — standard gaps, horizontal button padding.
- `--space-section` `1.5rem` — 8px grid tier 3 — section spacing, large gaps.
- `--z-sticky` `10` — Z-index scale (Pillar 3) — sticky headers and toolbars.
- `--z-nav` `30` — navbar — floats above sticky headers, below overlays.
- `--z-overlay` `40` — Z-index scale (Pillar 3) — dimming overlays and backdrops.
- `--z-modal` `50` — Z-index scale (Pillar 3) — modals, popups, dropdowns.
- `--z-toast` `60` — toasts — the zenith: above modals (1.4.0 Input & Feedback Layer).

### The Chromatic Palette (content-ONLY — the Rule of Engagement)

- `--sig-pink-bright` `#ea76cb` — Chromatic pink (bright) — high-emphasis content accent: badges, tag fills, event highlights.
- `--sig-pink-soft` `#f5bde6` — Chromatic pink (soft) — quiet content accent: tag surfaces, avatar rings, soft calendar fills.
- `--sig-pink-alt` `#f4b8e4` — Chromatic pink (alt) — alternate pink for content category differentiation.
- `--sig-mauve-bright` `#9e5ff2` — Chromatic mauve (bright) — high-contrast content accent: chart series, bold tags. 2.9.1 contrast fix: was #8839ef (2.32:1 on surface); lightened in-family (H266/S85 kept, L 58→66%, the minimal step ≥3.1) to 3.22:1 on surface / 4.20:1 on base. 3.6.0 two-tier policy: 3.22:1 measures ≥3.0 but <4.5 → declared DISPLAY tier — use at ≥1.5rem/600, as fills, borders or series strokes; never body text. VALUE FROZEN.
- `--sig-mauve-soft` `#cba6f7` — Chromatic mauve (soft) — quiet content accent: avatar dots, calendar blocks.
- `--sig-lavender` `#7287fd` — Chromatic lavender — content accent for links-in-content, calendar themes, data-viz series. 3.6.0 two-tier policy: 3.95:1 on surface measures ≥3.0 but <4.5 → declared DISPLAY tier — use at ≥1.5rem/600, as fills, borders or series strokes; never body text. VALUE FROZEN.
- `--sig-sky` `#04a5e5` — Chromatic sky — content accent for informational tags and data-viz series.
- `--sig-cobalt` `#89b4fa` — Chromatic cobalt — 3.0.0: --sig-blue RETIRED, value carried. The official Catppuccin Mocha Blue under its own name (5.97:1 on surface / 7.79:1 on base) — an ink-floor token, cleared for high-emphasis content accents. The old name is banned from css/, tokens.json and the whitelist.

**Rule of Engagement (non-negotiable):** `--sig-*` is content-only; Flamingo/Teal (`--color-cake-primary` / `--color-cake-secondary`) is structural-only. The two families never cross.

## The Multi-Theme Surface Engine (3.2.0)

The canonical theme mechanism: `data-sig-theme` on `<html>` — absent or "mocha" = the :root default; "oled" = true-black; "daylight" = high-contrast light. The legacy `<html data-theme="latte">` light toggle keeps working, outside the triad. Every theme is WCAG-gated per surface by the contrast engine; the manifest mirrors the css (cross-checked).

| theme | attribute | --bg-base | --bg-surface | --bg-inset | text |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Mocha (default) | absent / mocha | #1E1E2E | #313244 | #282A36 | #CDD6F4 family |
| OLED true-black | data-sig-theme="oled" | #000000 | #0B0C10 | #12141C | inherits #CDD6F4 (≥13.5:1) |
| Daylight | data-sig-theme="daylight" | #F8FAFC | #FFFFFF | #F1F5F9 | dark slate ink |

OLED declares ONLY the bg trio — everything else inherits (ratios only increase on true black). Daylight re-inks the chromatic family for white:

### Geometry Presets (the data-sig-radius axis)

- standard: `--radius-ui: 8px` · `--radius-card: 12px` (8px-grid-pure — 6px never was)
- sharp: `--radius-ui: 0px` · `--radius-card: 0px` (brutalist)

:root keeps the 6px/12px defaults — an absent attribute renders the historical look. Radius and color are orthogonal axes.

## The Kinetic Motion Tokens (3.7.0)



| token | value |
|---|---|
| `--ease-spring-snappy` | `linear(0, 0.44 6.4%, 0.83 12.9%, 1.02 18.6%, 1.08 24.2%, 1.09 28.9%, 1.05 34.9%, 0.98 42.4%, 0.97 48.5%, 1.01 58.6%, 1 69.1%, 1)` (fallback: `cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.56, 0.64, 1)`) |
| `--ease-spring-gentle` | `linear(0, 0.36 8.9%, 0.68 17.9%, 0.9 26.1%, 1.01 34.9%, 1.06 44.4%, 1.05 55.4%, 0.99 69.1%, 1)` (fallback: `cubic-bezier(0.25, 1.25, 0.45, 1)`) |
| `--ease-kinetic-out` | `linear(0, 0.61 10.8%, 0.91 22.7%, 1.02 34.3%, 1.05 45.5%, 1.01 61.4%, 1)` (fallback: `cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)`) |
| `--ease-glide` | `linear(0, 0.63 14.5%, 0.95 30.2%, 1.02 42.5%, 0.99 57.1%, 1)` (fallback: `cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1)`) |
| `--dur-spring-snappy` | `calc(var(--sig-motion-scale, 1) * 320ms)` |
| `--dur-spring-gentle` | `calc(var(--sig-motion-scale, 1) * 480ms)` |
| `--dur-kinetic-out` | `calc(var(--sig-motion-scale, 1) * 380ms)` |
| `--dur-glide` | `calc(var(--sig-motion-scale, 1) * 280ms)` |
| `--sig-motion-scale` | `1` |

## The Rules (The Dynamic Signature Engine v3.2)

# System Instruction: The Dynamic Signature Engine v4.0 — Full-Page Layout Templates, Interactive Viewport Previewer & CLI Template Expansion (Standalone Identity)

Act as my UI/UX Design Engine. I am building a project using my personal "Signature Style." You will act as a factory that takes plain code and injects this exact styling, scaling it dynamically so I do not have to do heavy manual setup.

## The Aesthetic & Theme:
A Catppuccin-mapped minimalist environment built for human eye comfort, inspired by a Linux terminal's calm. The default theme is Catppuccin Mocha (dark): soft dark blues for structure and official Catppuccin accents for interactions. A light "white version" — Catppuccin Latte — is available by opting in with `<html data-theme="latte">`; never author a third palette. It must look deliberate, ergonomic, and handcrafted, completely avoiding a generic AI-generated aesthetic.

**Harmonized Doctrine:** 100% official Catppuccin, per-theme — the dark toggle wears Mocha Flamingo/Teal, the light toggle wears Latte Flamingo/Teal. No cross-theme imports, no custom accents: harmony is mathematical by construction.

## The Core Design Tokens (The Base System):
Harmonized mapping (the dark default — Catppuccin Mocha, 100% official palette):
- --bg-base: #1E1E2E (Mocha base — page and app background)
- --bg-surface: #313244 (Mocha surface — cards, inputs, secondary buttons)
- --color-cake-primary: #F2CDCD (Mocha Flamingo — official signature, primary actions)
- --color-cake-secondary: #94E2D5 (Mocha Teal — official signature, focus rings, secondary accents)
- --text-main: #CDD6F4 (Mocha text — primary text)
- --text-muted: #7F849C (Mocha overlay — subtitles, hints, disabled labels)

Per-theme harmony: the Latte light theme wears its own official counterparts —
--color-cake-primary: #DD7878 (Latte Flamingo) and --color-cake-secondary: #179299 (Latte Teal).
Never import a Mocha accent into Latte or vice versa; each theme uses its own palette pairing.

Z-index scale (Pillar 3, theme-independent, same in both themes):
- --z-sticky: 10 / --z-overlay: 40 / --z-modal: 50

Keeper tokens (beloved legacy colors with semantic jobs):
- --bg-inset: #282A36 (inset wells, code blocks, input interiors)
- --text-bright: #F8F8F2 (maximum-contrast emphasis text, headings)
- --color-success: #A8E6CF (success actions)
- --text-muted-soft: #6272A4 (tertiary text, quiet captions)

Shared, theme-independent tokens:
- --color-on-cake: #1E1E2E (text/icon color on top of cake-colored surfaces)
- --font-sans: 'Inter', system-ui, sans-serif
- --radius-ui: 6px (minimalist corners)
- --transition-standard: all 0.15s ease-out
- --transition-transform: transform 0.3s cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.8, 0.2, 1)
- --space-tight: 0.5rem / --space-standard: 1rem / --space-section: 1.5rem (the 8px grid)

## The Multi-Theme Surface Engine (3.2.0):
The surface is a VERIFIED AXLE, not a hardcoded palette: the canonical theme mechanism is the `data-sig-theme` attribute on `<html>`, and the geometry axis rides `data-sig-radius`. Three surface themes — all WCAG-gated per theme by the contrast engine (every ink measured against that theme's own surface; the manifest `tokens.json → sigThemes` mirrors the css, and the contrast gate cross-checks the two):

| theme | attribute | --bg-base | --bg-surface | --bg-inset | text |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Mocha (default) | absent or `data-sig-theme="mocha"` | #1E1E2E | #313244 | #282A36 | #CDD6F4 family |
| OLED true-black | `data-sig-theme="oled"` | #000000 | #0B0C10 | #12141C | inherits #CDD6F4 (reads ≥13.5:1) |
| Daylight high-contrast | `data-sig-theme="daylight"` | #F8FAFC | #FFFFFF | #F1F5F9 | #0F172A / #020617 / #475569 / #64748B |

- **Inheritance is the mechanism:** OLED declares ONLY the background trio — every other token (the chromatic 26 included) inherits `:root`, and the ratios only increase on true black (worst fill 4.68:1 ≥ the 3.1 bar). NEVER re-declare inherited tokens in a theme block.
- **The daylight ink variants:** the chromatic family is RE-INKED for white — each override computed with the WCAG engine to measure ≥ 3.1:1 against #FFFFFF (the strictest daylight surface). Glows and luminous tints darken substantially (yellow #F9E2AF → amber #A16207; lime-glow #DBFF9E → #3F6212; rose-glow → #BE185D; mint-glow → #047857; cyan → #0E7490); saturated mids that already clear the bar on white (crimson, azure, tangerine, magenta, mauve-bright, lavender) inherit untouched. Every override documents its measured ratio in css/tokens.css comments AND `tokens.json → sigThemes.daylight.inkVariants` — the two are cross-checked; never hand-tune a variant without recomputing the ratio.
- **Cakes stay official:** the daylight wears the same pastel Flamingo/Teal fills carrying dark ink — `--color-on-cake` stays #1E1E2E (11.24:1 on #F2CDCD).
- **Geometry presets:** `data-sig-radius="standard"` retunes the radius axis to 8px UI / 12px cards (8px-GRID-PURE — the legacy 6px never snapped to the grid); `"sharp"` is the brutalist 0px/0px. The `:root` defaults stay 6px/12px — an absent attribute renders the historical look, byte-stable. Radius and color are orthogonal axes; the presets compose with any theme.
- **Legacy:** the old light toggle `<html data-theme="latte">` keeps working untouched — it is the LEGACY mechanism, outside the canonical triad; never author new work against it.
- **The live customizer:** the playground's Pattern Studio carries the Theme & Surface Customizer panel (also reachable via the ⌘K palette: "Theme: Mocha/OLED/Daylight", "Radius: Standard/Sharp", "Download tokens.css", "Copy CSS Variables"). Theme + radius persist as ONE merged object under `sig.workspace.v3.prefs` (`{ theme, radius }`; the v3.2.0 per-axis keys survive as a one-time migration read — an old pick is adopted on first load). "Copy Theme Snippet" puts the canonical `<html data-sig-theme="…" data-sig-radius="…">` line on the clipboard. Until the user picks (now or in a pre-3.6.0 session), BOTH attributes stay ABSENT (the mocha/6px legacy look). Contrast badges render the 16 chromatic tokens for the ACTIVE theme with the same WCAG math the gate uses.

## Scaffolding (3.3.0 — the npx init CLI):
New projects don't hand-wire tokens anymore: `npx @edwyn/signature-style init` scaffolds a resolved `signature-tokens.css` (one of the three themes + the standard geometry preset, zero dependencies) and, with `--template bento`, a standalone 12-column starter that already obeys every pillar on this page. The CLI's embedded theme map is drift-gated against `css/tokens.css` by `verify:cli` (cli2) — when scaffolding, the palette you get IS this document's palette. Prefer the CLI for fresh surfaces; hand-injection stays reserved for retrofits.

## Full-Page Layout Blueprints (3.8.0 — the capstone):
The engine now scaffolds ENTIRE SITES: three self-contained full-page templates — one default-export React page each, composed exclusively from `@edwyn/signature-style/react` exports + the kinetic primitives, carrying an embedded token-driven `<style>` block (zero hex, 8px grid, container queries so the page answers its CONTAINER width, reduced-motion honored). In the playground's Templates Studio (`#/templates`) each blueprint previews live inside the viewport emulator (Desktop 100% / Tablet 768px / Mobile 375px), re-themes under the SCOPED switcher (`data-sig-theme` on the stage wrapper — the theme blocks are plain attribute selectors, so a div re-themes its subtree), and copies as full TSX. The CLI emits the same pages: `vite-react`/`next` hosts get the React blueprint; `html`/`fresh` hosts get a per-template STATIC HTML MIRROR (the same blocks as plain HTML + the tokens variables — one honest snapshot, not the React statefulness). The registry: `playground/template-registry.ts` → `PAGE_TEMPLATES` (`id` / `name` / `description` / `Component` / `source` — the source strings are the formatted standalone TSX, mechanically derived, so the copy payload can never drift).

### Blueprint 01 — SaaS Landing (`saas`):
Block-by-block: (1) `AnnouncementBanner` release rail (badge copy + action button) → (2) centered `PageHero` in a staggered `MotionReveal` entrance, then the dual `Button` CTAs (primary + secondary) on the 45ms stagger wave → (3) 3-column feature grid of `KineticSurface` cards (cursor-tracking sheen; 40px icon wells tinted `color-mix(in srgb, var(--sig-token) 12%, transparent)`) → (4) the billing switcher: `Tabs` (Monthly | Annual — Save 20%) with the FLIP indicator driving one `billing` state, a live `AnimatedNumber` price strip recomputing (annual = 20% off computed) above the 3-column `TierCard` row (Starter $19 · Pro $49 featured elevation · Enterprise $199) → (5) three `AccordionCard` FAQ entries → (6) structured footer (brand + three nav columns + fineprint). State: `billing` via `useState`; the price `AnimatedNumber` recomputes on the cycle flip. CLI: `npx @edwyn/signature-style init --template saas`.

Entry snippet:
```tsx
import SaasLandingTemplate from "./SignatureSaasLanding";
// entry.tsx — once, before your own styles:
// import "@edwyn/signature-style/css";
<SaasLandingTemplate />
```

### Blueprint 02 — Docs Reader (`docs`):
Block-by-block: (1) `Breadcrumbs` (engine / docs / getting-started) → (2) THE 3-COLUMN GRID — 220px chapter tree | `minmax(0, 1fr)` reading column | 200px "On This Page" outline, collapsing to one column below a 1023px CONTAINER (`@container tpl-docs`; container preferred over media queries so the stage emulator reflows it) → (3) chapter tree: a nav list with a `useState` active chapter over real section anchors → (4) the reading column: `ProseBlock` sections (h3 + paragraphs + one blockquote — the --sig-violet-glow bar), the info `Callout` ("This page is a live template."), the `ReferenceCard` (tag "TSX", the copyable setup snippet, `onCopied` wired to the toast) and the configuration-reference `DataTable` (5 rows) → (5) the outline: a STATIC list built from the section headings (kept honest — no scroll-spy) → (6) Prev/Next `ActionTile` pager. State: `activeChapter` via `useState`. CLI: `npx @edwyn/signature-style init --template docs`.

Entry snippet:
```tsx
import DocsReaderTemplate from "./SignatureDocsReader";
// entry.tsx — once, before your own styles:
// import "@edwyn/signature-style/css";
<DocsReaderTemplate />
```

### Blueprint 03 — Telemetry Center (`telemetry`):
Block-by-block: the asymmetric 12-column bento — (1) KPI row: four span-3 tiles (two LIVE tiles composing `AnimatedNumber` rolling readouts + `Sparkline`; two package `StatCard`s — StatCard.value is a string contract, so the rolling tiles compose the primitives into the StatCard anatomy) → (2) two `StatRing` capacity gauges (total + unit: the zoom/detail strip) → (3) `AreaChart` + `BarChart` in `SurfaceCard` panels, side by side (span 6 + span 6) → (4) the deployment schedule: `TimelineManager` fully wired to local state (composer, settle toggles, deletes) → (5) the node status ledger: a `DataTable` filtered live by an `Input` (case-insensitive substring over node/status/region, `useMemo` derivative). State: deployments via `useState`, the filter query via `useState`; every derived row list is a `useMemo` over the current state (causal by construction). CLI: `npx @edwyn/signature-style init --template telemetry`.

Entry snippet:
```tsx
import TelemetryCenterTemplate from "./SignatureTelemetryCenter";
// entry.tsx — once, before your own styles:
// import "@edwyn/signature-style/css";
<TelemetryCenterTemplate />
```

## Web Components (Zero-React Surface) (3.4.0):
The same Signature Style as **six framework-free custom elements** for Vue/Svelte/HTML/any-stack (and for AI agents generating vanilla code). Plain TypeScript `HTMLElement` subclasses — **zero runtime dependencies** (no React, no Lit), one shadow-DOM `<slot>` anatomy each — registered by ONE module import and themed by ONE stylesheet link:

- **Tokens prerequisite (read first):** the elements ship NO colors. Link `@edwyn/signature-style/css` (or the CLI's `signature-tokens.css`) ONCE — the `--sig-*` custom properties **inherit through shadow-DOM boundaries** (custom properties inherit; shadow roots don't block them), so the link themes all six elements, `<html data-sig-theme="daylight">` included.
- **Registration:** `import "@edwyn/signature-style/wc";` — defines all six (guarded: already-registered names are skipped). Imperative classes + types ride the same module (`import { SigStatRing } from "@edwyn/signature-style/wc"`).

| Element | Attributes | Shadow-DOM shape | React twin |
|---|---|---|---|
| `<sig-surface-card>` | `eyebrow` · `meta` · `title` · `accent-token` (--sig-* or structural) · `elevation="flat\|raised\|floating"` (default raised) · `interactive` | meta row (teal/accent all-caps eyebrow + muted mono path) → ruled title (2px accent underline when `accent-token` present) → default `<slot>`; the elevation-tier ambient shadows live ONLY on the inner `.card` (the e1 sanction, mirrored inside the shadow) | `<SurfaceCard>` |
| `<sig-badge>` | `label` · `variant` (peach/sky/green/cobalt/lavender/mauve-soft/pink-bright/yellow/orchid) · `accent-token` (wins) | one flat pill — tint/border derived by `color-mix` from the token; no shadow, ever | `<SigBadge>` |
| `<sig-progress-bar>` | `value` · `max` (default 100) · `label` (→ aria-label) · `limit-text` · `accent-token` | track (bg-inset + hairline) + fill (accent or --sig-cobalt, width 0.3s ease-out) + tabular mono caption; host carries `role="progressbar"` + `aria-valuenow` recomputed per render | `<ProgressBar>` |
| `<sig-stat-ring>` | `value` · `total` · `unit` (default "%") · `size` (default 120) · `accent-token` · `show-value` | pure SVG: track circle (bg-inset) + progress arc (accent) + boundary hairline over the ink + centered tabular "{value}%" readout; a `value` change animates `stroke-dashoffset` (transition inside the shadow sheet; `prefers-reduced-motion` honored there too) | `<StatRing>` |
| `<sig-callout>` | `status="info\|success\|warning"` (default info) | 4px left strip (sky/green/peach) over the inset well, `role="note"`, body slotted; never auto-dismisses | `<Callout>` |
| `<sig-carousel>` | `mode="free\|paged"` (default free) · `label` | scroll-snap track wrapping a default `<slot>` + docked control bar (Prev · dots · Next · tabular "1 / N" aria-live); N grows from the `slotchange` assigned-node count; paged advances one track width, free one item; track is keyboard-reachable (Arrow keys drive the buttons) | `<Carousel>` |

- **Vanilla usage** (any stack — this is valid JSX too):
  ```html
  <sig-surface-card eyebrow="Telemetry" title="Attendance Pulse" accent-token="--sig-peach" elevation="floating" interactive>
    <p>Slot body</p>
  </sig-surface-card>
  <sig-stat-ring value="85" accent-token="--sig-cobalt"></sig-stat-ring>
  ```
  Attributes only — no props, no events, no framework runtime. `setAttribute("value", "40")` is the whole reactive story.
- **The RoE holds inside the shadows:** every shadow style string is 100% `var()`/`color-mix` (zero hex); `--sig-*` accents paint content only (badge variants, ring arcs, callout strips, card underlines) — never structural chrome. The e1 zero-shadow law is mirrored: the sanctioned ambient elevation shadows exist ONLY on the surface-card's inner `.card` element.

## The Visual Cortex as a Product (3.5.0):
The engine now SHIPS ITS OWN EYES: `packages/signature-mcp` — a standalone MCP stdio server (private `@edwyn/signature-mcp`, `bin: signature-mcp`) that gives any AI session spatial awareness of the RENDERED app — the AI can measure what it styles. Build: `npm --prefix packages/signature-mcp run build`; prerequisite: `npx playwright install chromium` once + the dev server (`npm run playground`, default `http://localhost:5173` — every tool degrades into a graceful error naming that command). Playwright is pinned EXACTLY to the repo's installed version (no second browser download). The four tools:

| Tool | Params | Returns |
|---|---|---|
| `inspect_layout` | `url?` · `selectors?` (default the 28-selector anatomy sweep) | per-element `{selector, tag, classes, rect, text, visible}` + per-class coverage |
| `audit_contrast` | `url?` · `selectors?` · `minRatio?` (default 3.0) | per-element `{selector, fg, bg, ratio, pass}` — effective background = first painted ancestor → body/html → the documented `#1E1E2E` assumption; worst-first failure summary |
| `audit_e1_shadows` | `url?` | every computed box-shadow with an `allowed` verdict (the e1 sanction: `.sig-surface-card` / `.sig-card` / `[data-elevation]`) + violations list + sanctioned count — the e1 treaty OPERATIONALIZED at runtime |
| `capture_viewport_matrix` | `url?` · `viewports?` (default 375×812 · 768×1024 · 1440×900 · 1920×1080) · `fullPage?` · `path?` | flat matrix `[{viewport, path, bytes}]` — one PNG per viewport |

- **Attach configs** (full copies in `packages/signature-mcp/README.md`): VS Code `.vscode/mcp.json` (`servers` shape), Claude Code (`claude mcp add signature-mcp -- node <abs>/packages/signature-mcp/dist/server.js` + the `mcpServers` JSON), OpenCode V2 `opencode.json` (`mcp.servers`, <https://opencode.ai/docs/mcp-servers>). All point at `node <abs>/packages/signature-mcp/dist/server.js`.
- **The certifications** (the CI story): `verify:mcp` (the raw JSON-RPC smoke — exactly the four tools, layout hits, contrast summary, e1 verdicts, 4 viewport paths), `verify:a11y` (3.6.0 Zero-Defect A11y: keyboard tab-order across ALL views + the doctrine focus halo ≥2px in `var(--color-cake-primary)` — the exception table is EMPTY, the master-index gateway doors wear the real ring — + the toast live region + the role census + the INERT SWEEP (hidden means inert: the FlipCard faces swap, the aria-hidden probe fixture is inert, the closed `<details>` contract asserted) + axe ZERO critical/serious/moderate on every view, with color-contrast ADJUDICATED by the two-tier policy — every axe-flagged pair must still measure ≥3.0:1 or the gate fails), `verify:contrast` (3.6.0 TWO-TIER: ink-tier tokens ≥4.5:1 for body text, display-tier ≥3.0:1 — mauve-bright 3.22 / lavender 3.95 / peach 4.22 / --text-muted 3.40 classified DISPLAY by `tokens.json → doctrine.contrastPolicy` + per-token `contrastTier` metadata, VALUES byte-frozen; the gate cross-checks the metadata, ct8), `verify:visual-diff` (pixelmatch golden masters of the SEVEN views at 1440×900, 0.1% tolerance — `update:snapshots` regenerates; font-dependent by nature, so CI runs it `continue-on-error` while LOCAL runs are the strict gate), `verify:examples` (python3 py_compile on the fastapi-starter trio + the pack-proof — examples/ never rides the tarball). `.github/workflows/ci.yml` wires the suites in parallel jobs on every push/PR. The retired `tools/mcp-viz/` inspector lives on INSIDE the package verbatim.

## The Chromatic Palette (Content-Only Tokens):
Twenty-six theme-independent CONTENT colors (v2.4 origin; 2.5.0 adds --sig-yellow, the strength meter's Fair stage; 2.9.1 re-inks mauve-bright for zero contrast debt; 3.0.0 the 16-color expansion — --sig-blue RETIRES, its value surviving as --sig-cobalt; 3.1.0 the --sig-* rename; 3.2.0 adds the daylight ink variants; 3.6.0 the TWO-TIER contrast policy — every ink-family token carries a `contrastTier` in tokens.json: "ink" tokens are body-text-clear at ≥4.5:1, the sub-4.5 inks — mauve-bright 3.22:1, lavender 3.95:1, peach 4.22:1, --text-muted 3.40:1 — are classified DISPLAY tier: use at ≥1.5rem/600, as borders, fills, badges or caption metadata, NEVER body text; values stay frozen, the policy documents the tier and the gates enforce it), defined ONCE in `:root` and inherited by every surface theme untouched (daylight re-inks 20 of them — see the Multi-Theme Surface Engine above):

The legacy eleven (suffix names):
- --sig-pink-bright: #ea76cb (badges, tag fills, event highlights)
- --sig-pink-soft: #f5bde6 (tag surfaces, avatar rings, soft calendar fills)
- --sig-pink-alt: #f4b8e4 (alternate pink for content categories)
- --sig-mauve-bright: #9e5ff2 (chart series, bold tags — 2.9.1: was #8839ef, a 2.32:1 sub-floor FAIL)
- --sig-mauve-soft: #cba6f7 (avatar dots, calendar blocks)
- --sig-lavender: #7287fd (content links, calendar themes, data-viz series)
- --sig-sky: #04a5e5 (informational tags, data-viz series)
- --sig-cobalt: #89b4fa (data-viz series, event themes — 3.0.0: the retired --sig-blue's exact value, the official Mocha Blue under its own name; the old name is banned)
- --sig-peach: #fe640b (calendar block edges, attention tags)
- --sig-green: #a6d189 (status tags, positive data-viz series)
- --sig-yellow: #F9E2AF (the strength meter's Fair stage — feedback meter stages, owner v2.5.0)

The chromatic fifteen (3.0.0 — DECLARED fill/series accents: bars, node rings, borders, tinted wells; every value ≥2.0:1 vs --bg-surface, floor leader crimson 3.01:1):
- --sig-orchid: #F5C2E7 · --sig-cyan: #64DFDF · --sig-magenta: #CF64DF · --sig-mint: #64DF99 · --sig-spring: #6EDF64 · --sig-citron: #DBDF64
- --sig-violet-glow: #C29EFF · --sig-pink-glow: #F29EFF · --sig-rose-glow: #FF9EDB · --sig-lime-glow: #DBFF9E · --sig-mint-glow: #9EFFC2
- --sig-crimson: #F22222 · --sig-azure: #228AF2 · --sig-tangerine: #F25622 · --sig-neon-green: #56F222

**Rule of Engagement (non-negotiable):** `--sig-*` tokens are reserved EXCLUSIVELY for content — badges, tags, avatars, event theme overrides, calendar blocks, data visualization. The Engine continues using Flamingo/Teal (`--color-cake-primary` / `--color-cake-secondary`) for ALL structural UI actions — buttons, inputs, focus rings. Never use `--sig-*` for structural chrome; never use Flamingo/Teal for content categories. The two families never cross.

## The Token Cascade (Fixing Heavy Setup):
Do not ask me for hover, active, disabled, or focus states. You must dynamically calculate them using modern CSS (color-mix(), transforms) based strictly on the Core Tokens.
- Hover states: Lighten the core token slightly (`color-mix(… 85%, white)`) or increase opacity.
- Active states: Darken the token (`color-mix(… 85%, black)`) AND press the element with `transform: scale(0.97)`.
- Disabled states: Convert the element to --bg-surface, use --text-muted to gray it out, and cancel the transform.
- Focus-visible: `outline: 2px solid var(--color-cake-primary); outline-offset: 2px` — never a color token swap on the ring.

## The Override Protocol (Fixing Rigidity):
Maintain absolute consistency 95% of the time using the Provider Pattern. However, if I explicitly ask for a unique color or shape for a specific component (e.g., "Make this warning button bright red"), you are authorized to create a scoped CSS utility class (e.g., .btn-override-danger) that alters that specific element locally. Never change the global variables to achieve this. The classics stay canonical: danger keeps the bright red #FF6B6B, gold keeps its #FFD700→#DAA520 gradient, success rides --color-success.

## The Structural Pillars (Non-Negotiable):
1. **Iconography** — Lucide-React exclusively. The 2px stroke matches Inter weight 500 exactly. Never mix icon libraries; if a component needs an icon, it comes from Lucide or it does not exist.
2. **Breakpoints** — strict mobile shift at `max-width: 768px`. Every multi-column grid collapses to a single column at that width; there are no other breakpoints.
3. **Z-Index Scale** — sticky headers/toolbars at z-10 (`--z-sticky`), dimming overlays/backdrops at z-40 (`--z-overlay`), modals/popups/dropdowns at z-50 (`--z-modal`). No ad-hoc z-index values, no z-index arms races.
4. **Edge States** — loading is a pulsing-opacity skeleton on `--bg-surface` (opacity 1 → 0.5 → 1, ~1.5s ease-in-out, `animation: none` under prefers-reduced-motion); empty is a `--bg-surface` card with a Lucide icon and `--text-muted` text, centered on both axes.

## The Pruning Protocol (Subtract by Default):
Before you write a line of code, ask what line you can delete instead. The owner's mandate:
- **Subtract by Default:** You are explicitly authorized and encouraged to delete redundant code.
- **DOM Flattening:** Never use a wrapper `<div>` if CSS Flexbox/Grid on the parent can achieve the same layout. If an element looks visually identical without a wrapper, delete the wrapper.
- **Minimalist Code:** Do not add "extra stuff" or decorative wrappers. If the UI looks clean and functions correctly with 3 lines of HTML instead of 10, use 3.

When you ship React, prefer the official primitives in this package — `<Icon>`, `<EmptyState>`, and `<SigBadge>` from `@edwyn/signature-style/react` — over hand-rolled equivalents. They already follow every pillar above; a hand-rolled copy is redundant code, and redundant code gets pruned.

## The 6-Set Taxonomy — every component, copy-paste

Registry: 56 entries, one per value export of react/index.d.ts, plus the Set 08 motion registry (10 entries). Every snippet is compile-plausible documentation — one import, no invented props.

### Set 01 — Shell & Navigation

The frame every view hangs in: one centered column, one announcing hero, one sticky nav. Reach for this set first — layout is the doctrine everything else composes into.

#### ThemeProvider (ThemeProvider)

Copy-paste JSX:

```tsx

<ThemeProvider theme={{ "--color-cake-primary": "#F2CDCD" }}>
  <App />
</ThemeProvider>
```

Props surface — react/ThemeProvider.d.ts (`ThemeProviderProps`):

```ts
export interface ThemeProviderProps {
    /** Token overrides. Values must be plain CSS values (no `{`, `}`, `;`, `\`). */
    theme?: ThemeOverrides;
    children?: ReactNode;
}
```

#### GlobalNav (GlobalNav)

```tsx

const items = [{ href: "#/dashboard", label: "Dashboard" }];
<GlobalNav items={items} activeHref="#/dashboard" />
```

Props surface — react/nav.d.ts (`GlobalNavProps`):

```ts
export interface GlobalNavProps {
    /** The navigation destinations, rendered once in the bar and in the drawer. */
    items: NavItem[];
    /**
     * Component-agnostic link renderer: pass React Router's NavLink;
     * defaults to <a>. Receives { href, className, children, 'aria-current'? }.
     */
    as?: ElementType;
    /**
     * Which href is the current page (sets aria-current="page"). With
     * React Router + NavLink, the router sets it — leave undefined.
     */
    activeHref?: string;
}
```

export interface TabsProps {

    tabs: TabsTab[];

### Set 02 — Surface & Card Archetypes

The surfaces people actually read: heroes, cards, badges and the five universal archetypes. Content colors live here — chromatic tokens paint the categories, Flamingo/Teal never do.

#### SurfaceCard (SurfaceCard)

Copy-paste JSX:

```tsx
import { SurfaceCard } from "@edwyn/signature-style/react";

<SurfaceCard eyebrow="Forms" meta="components/forms.tsx" title="Form Controls" interactive>
  <Input placeholder="Member name" />
</SurfaceCard>
<SurfaceCard
  eyebrow="Workbench" meta="views/workbench.tsx" title="Bento Workbench"
  interactive accentToken="--color-cake-primary" elevation="floating"
>

</SurfaceCard>
```

Props surface — react/surface.d.ts (`SurfaceCardProps`):

```ts
export interface SurfaceCardProps {
    /** Teal all-caps eyebrow label (left half of the meta row). */
    eyebrow?: string;
    /** Muted mono source path (right half of the meta row). */
    meta?: string;
    /** The ruled card title (h2). */
    title?: string;
    /** The tactile hover: translateY(-2px) + deepened ambient shadow. */
    interactive?: boolean;
    /**
     * The chromatic accent (2.6.0): a `--sig-*` content token or one of
     * the two structural signatures. Colors the eyebrow + the ruled title
     * underline (2px solid — the GlobalNav/Tabs contract) and tints the
     * interactive hover glow. Omit for the classic teal/muted card.
     */
    accentToken?: AccentToken;
    /**
     * The shadow tier (2.6.0, default "raised"): "flat" — border hairline
     * only, zero shadow; "raised" — the historical ambient (values tuned
     * to 0.06 inset / 0.42 ambient); "floating" — the deep display shadow
     * (interactive hover lifts -4px).
     */
    elevation?: SurfaceElevation;
    /** Extra classes composed ON the primitive (e.g. grid placement). */
    className?: string;
    /** The card content — rendered directly inside the section. */
    children?: ReactNode;
}
```

#### ProfileCard (ProfileCard)

import { ProfileCard } from "@edwyn/signature-style/react";

<ProfileCard
  name="Ana Souza" role="Head of Catering" accentToken="--sig-peach"
  stats={[
    { label: "Events", value: "24" },
    { label: "Members", value: "412" },
    { label: "Rating", value: "4.9" },
  ]}
  skills={[
    { colorToken: "--sig-peach", label: "Catering" },
    { colorToken: "--sig-green", label: "Logistics" },
  ]}
/>
```

Props surface — react/cards.d.ts (`ProfileCardProps`):

```ts
export interface ProfileCardProps {
    /** The person's name — the Avatar's initials AND the headline. */
    name: string;
    /** The muted role line (0.8125rem). */
    role: string;
    /** Two to three {label, value} stats (tabular values, muted labels). */
    stats?: ProfileStat[];
    /** Skill badges (SigBadges) on the last row. */
    skills?: ProfileSkill[];
    /** The `--sig-*` token for the avatar ring (content-only rule). */
    accentToken?: SigColorToken;
    /** Avatar diameter (32 | 40, default 40 — the grid-perfect pair). */
    avatarSize?: 32 | 40;
    /** Passthrough classes for grid placement. */
    className?: string;
}
```

### Set 03 — Ergonomic Forms & Inputs

Format rules sit above the input so people read the constraint before typing — announced by screen readers in the same breath as the label. Errors are states, not popups; every control keeps its native semantics.

#### FormField (FormField)

Copy-paste JSX:

```tsx
import { FormField, Input } from "@edwyn/signature-style/react";

<FormField
  label="Postal Code"
  htmlFor="zip"
  description="5 numbers only · e.g., 79901"
  validMessage={/^\d{5}$/.test(zip) ? "Valid ZIP" : undefined}
  error={zip !== "" && !/^\d{5}$/.test(zip) ? "Postal codes are 5 digits" : undefined}
>
  <Input id="zip" inputMode="numeric" value={zip} onChange={(e) => setZip(e.target.value)} />
</FormField>
<FormField label="Contribution" htmlFor="share" prefix="$" required hint="Suggested $50">
  <Input id="share" required inputMode="numeric" value={share} onChange={(e) => setShare(e.target.value)} />
</FormField>
```

Props surface — react/forms.d.ts (`FormFieldProps`):

```ts
export interface FormFieldProps {
    /** The visible label text (rendered in the `.sig-form-field__label`). */
    label: string;
    /**
     * The control's `id` — YOU also pass it to the child control; this
     * prop only wires the label's `htmlFor` to it.
     */
    htmlFor?: string;
    /**
     * The muted FORMAT line ABOVE the control (2.5.0), directly below the
     * title — e.g. "5 numbers only · e.g., 79901". This is where format
     * rules live (the v2.4.1 defect: rules under the input read as an
     * error). NOT the hint: `hint` stays the below-input helper text for
     * non-format context.
     */
    description?: string;
    /**
     * The muted helper line UNDER the control (unchanged 2.4.0 semantics).
     * LOSES the priority contest in the validation zone: error →
     * validMessage → hint, one line shown, never two.
     */
    hint?: string;
    /**
     * The error message — rendered with role="alert" (announced without a
     * focus change) and WINNING the validation zone. This is the MESSAGE
     * slot; the control's own error STATE is still `aria-invalid` (v1.4.0
     * doctrine). Wire them together: `error` here + `aria-invalid` on the
     * child. A truthy `error` also flips the well's `data-invalid`
     * attribute (peach border + the shake) when the control rides one.
     */
    error?: string;
    /**
     * The live-validation SUCCESS line (2.5.0) — rendered below the
     * control in `var(--sig-green)`, outranked only by `error`. The
     * "Valid ZIP" twin of the error slot: pass it when the value passes
     * your rule, e.g. `validMessage={/^\d{5}$/.test(postal) ? "Valid ZIP" : undefined}`.
     */
    validMessage?: string;
    /**
     * A literal adornment rendered BEFORE the control (2.4.1; 2.5.0
     * re-homed), e.g. `prefix="$"` for money fields. When prefix/suffix
     * are present the children are wrapped in the
     * `.sig-form-field__well` adornment zone (THE JUSTIFIED WRAPPER: an
     * adornment composition needs a flex parent that can own the border —
     * the bare control must stay untouched inside it) with the
     * `.sig-form-field__chip` mono span ahead of it. THE CONTRACT: the
     * children must be BARE inputs — the well owns the background,
     * border and focus ring (css/forms.css scopes
     * `.sig-form-field__well > .sig-input` kills). The adornment is
     * DECORATION — the value's currency belongs to the consumer's
     * placeholder/validation, never to the input's value. The chip is
     * separated from the cursor by a hairline, never glued into the label
     * (the second v2.4.1 defect: "$" concatenated into "Contribution").
     */
    prefix?: string;
    /**
     * A literal adornment rendered AFTER the control (2.5.0) — the mirror
     * of `prefix` (e.g. `suffix="kg"`), riding the same well as the right
     * chip. Same bare-input contract.
     */
    suffix?: string;
    /** The control (an `<Input>`, `<TextArea>`, `<Select>`, …). */
    children?: ReactNode;
    /**
     * Marks the field visually required (2.4.1): a `--sig-peach` `*`
     * renders AFTER the label text. VISUAL ONLY — the asterisk span is
     * aria-hidden and the FIELD renders no aria-required of its own;
     * the CONTROL owns that contract. Pass it on the child yourself,
     * e.g. `<Input required aria-required="true" …>` (native inputs
     * derive aria-required from `required`) — the wrapper never speaks
     * for a control it cannot verify, the same doctrine as id/htmlFor.
     */
    required?: boolean;
    /**
     * 3.0.0 — the ⓘ tooltip text. When present, an Info-icon button
     * renders beside the label (title + aria-label carry the text; the
     * visible tooltip is PURE CSS: a ::after bubble above the button,
     * shown on :hover AND :focus-visible — keyboard parity by
     * construction, zero dependencies). Tooltips are for non-critical
     * context; format rules stay in `description` (announced to screen
     * readers via aria-describedby — see the helpers slot).
     */
    infoTooltip?: string;
}
```

#### Input (Input)

Copy-paste JSX:

```tsx
import { Input } from "@edwyn/signature-style/react";

<Input
  value={name}
  onChange={(e) => setName(e.target.value)}
  error={name.length === 0 && "Name is required"}
  aria-describedby="name-error"
/>
```

HTML variant (no React — real package classes/inline styles):

```html
<input class="sig-input" type="text" placeholder="Member name" />
```

Props surface — react/forms.d.ts (`InputProps`):

```ts
export interface InputProps extends InputHTMLAttributes<HTMLInputElement> {
    /**
     * Error STATE flag — a boolean or a truthy string. Never rendered as
     * text: it only sets `aria-invalid="true"` on the element, which
     * css/forms.css answers with the --sig-peach error border. Render
     * your own message beside the field (wire its id via
     * aria-describedby yourself).
     */
    error?: boolean | string;
}
```

     * field.

export interface RadioCardGroupProps {

Props surface — react/forms.d.ts (`ToggleSwitchProps`):

```ts
export interface ToggleSwitchProps {
    /** Whether the switch is on (drives aria-checked → the Teal track). */
    checked: boolean;
    /** Called with the NEXT value on click: `onToggle(!checked)`. */
    onToggle?: (next: boolean) => void;
    /**
     * The switch's name — rendered as VISIBLE text beside the pill
     * (2.4.1; was aria-label only, which orphaned the control). The
     * pill stays the ONLY interactive element and keeps its aria-label,
     * so the accessible name never depends on the text span's DOM
     * position. Optional in the type, but every real switch should
     * name itself.
     */
    label?: string;
}
```

#### Button (Button)

Copy-paste JSX:

```tsx
import { Button } from "@edwyn/signature-style/react";

<Button variant="primary" size="md" leftIcon="Check" loading={submitting} type="submit">
  Check In
</Button>
<Button variant="danger" size="sm" onClick={remove}>Remove member</Button>
```

HTML variant (no React — real package classes/inline styles):

```html
<button class="sig-btn sig-btn--primary" type="submit">Check In</button>
<button class="sig-btn sig-btn--secondary" type="button">Maybe</button>
<button class="sig-btn sig-btn--ghost sig-btn--sm" type="button">Skip</button>
```

Props surface — react/primitives.d.ts (`ButtonProps`):

```ts
export interface ButtonProps extends ButtonHTMLAttributes<HTMLButtonElement> {
    /**
     * The visual variant (default "primary"):
     *  - primary — Flamingo fill, on-cake ink, weight 600. FLAT by
     *    package law: css/primitives.css carries ZERO box-shadow (the e1
     *    doctrine — elevation is a composition-layer decision; the
     *    playground shadows its own primary buttons there).
     *  - secondary — surface fill + hairline, text-main.
     *  - ghost — transparent; hover paints the inset well.
     *  - danger — the sig-peach attention wash (the error-border
     *    precedent: danger is attention, chromatic territory by owner spec).
     */
    variant?: "primary" | "secondary" | "ghost" | "danger";
    /**
     * Size tier (default "md"): sm → tight padding + 0.8125rem, md → the
     * doctrine button padding (tight vertical / standard horizontal) +
     * 0.875rem, lg → standard padding + 1rem.
     */
    size?: "sm" | "md" | "lg";
    /** A lucide icon rendered BEFORE the children. */
    leftIcon?: IconName;
    /** A lucide icon rendered AFTER the children. */
    rightIcon?: IconName;
    /**
     * The busy state: the icons are REPLACED by the
     * `.sig-btn__spinner` (aria-hidden), the button gains
     * `aria-busy="true"` and `disabled` — a loading button cannot be
     * re-submitted.
     */
    loading?: boolean;
}
```

### Set 04 — Analytical Telemetry & Graphs

The dashboards' math made visible: bars that admit their limits, rings that read at a glance, charts drawn as pure SVG with hover readouts. Reach for this set whenever a number deserves eyes — the colors stay content-only and the digits never jitter.

#### ProgressBar (ProgressBar)

Copy-paste JSX:

```tsx
import { ProgressBar } from "@edwyn/signature-style/react";

<ProgressBar value={72} colorToken="--sig-green" label="Budget remaining" limitText="$720 / $1,000" />
```

Props surface — react/viz.d.ts (`ProgressBarProps`):

```ts
export interface ProgressBarProps {
    /** The filled percentage — clamped to 0–100 before rendering. */
    value: number;
    /** A `--sig-*` content token — the ONLY tokens allowed here. */
    colorToken: SigTokenName;
    /** The accessible name for the progressbar (e.g. "Budget remaining"). */
    label?: string;
    /** 2.2.0: limit caption rendered after the track (e.g. "$1,325 / $2,000"). */
    limitText?: string;
}
```

#### StatRing (StatRing)

Copy-paste JSX:

```tsx
import { StatRing } from "@edwyn/signature-style/react";

<StatRing value={85} colorToken="--sig-sky" label="Attendance ratio" size="md" />
```

Props surface — react/viz.d.ts (`StatRingProps`):

```ts
export interface StatRingProps {
    /** The filled percentage — clamped to 0–100 before rendering. */
    value: number;
    /** A `--sig-*` content token — the ONLY tokens allowed here. */
    colorToken: SigTokenName;
    /**
     * 3.9.0 — the size ENUM ("sm" 88 / "md" 128 / "lg" 168), default
     * "md". BREAKING: was `number` (default 120). The px value lands as
     * `--ring-size` on the svg (css/viz.css answers with an exact square
     * that never stretches).
     */
    size?: StatRingSize;
    /** Track/fill weight in px — grid-perfect: 4 (half unit) or 8 (one unit). Default 8. */
    strokeWidth?: 4 | 8;
    /** 2.2.0: centered ring readout inside the SVG. Default true. */
    showValue?: boolean;
    /** The accessible name for the progressbar (e.g. "Attendance ratio"). */
    label?: string;
    /**
     * 3.0.0 — the denominator for the expandable detail strip (e.g. 200).
     * When present, the ring renders zoomable: hover/press scale(1.07),
     * and a click toggles the `.sig-ring__detail` strip below the ring —
     * "{value}% · {numerator}/{denominator} {unit}" with the numerator
     * derived from the value (85% of 200 → "170 / 200 Seats"). The core
     * dash geometry + the ARIA contract are untouched.
     */
    total?: number;
    /** 3.0.0 — the detail strip's unit label ("Seats"). Requires `total`. */
    unit?: string;
}
```

#### KnowledgeGraph (KnowledgeGraph)

Copy-paste JSX:

```tsx
import { KnowledgeGraph, type GraphNode } from "@edwyn/signature-style/react";

const nodes: GraphNode[] = [
  { id: "root", label: "Core Engine", categoryToken: "--sig-lavender", note: "Every branch is one layer." },
  { id: "venue", label: "Venue", parentId: "root", categoryToken: "--sig-mauve-soft" },
];

<KnowledgeGraph
  nodes={nodes}
  addOn
  onAddNode={(node) => addNode(node)}
  onSelectNode={(node) => inspect(node)}
  label="Workbench knowledge graph"
  height={320}
/>
```

Props surface — react/graph.d.ts (`KnowledgeGraphProps`):

```ts
export interface KnowledgeGraphProps {
    /** The nodes — order is irrelevant; the layout is id-hash deterministic. */
    nodes: GraphNode[];
    /** Called by the "Add & Link" toolbar with the new node (minus its id). */
    onAddNode?: (node: Omit<GraphNode, "id">) => void;
    /**
     * 3.0.0 — called by double-click on empty canvas with the graph-space
     * point and the parent hint (the nearest node, or the root).
     */
    onAddNodeAt?: (point: {
        x: number;
        y: number;
    }, parentId?: string) => void;
    /** Fired when a node is clicked/keyboard-activated (selection stays internal). */
    onSelectNode?: (node: GraphNode) => void;
    /**
     * 3.6.0 — fired when an edge is clicked (the hit path). The consumer
     * mirrors the selection into the inspector's edge card.
     */
    onSelectEdge?: (edge: GraphEdgeSelection) => void;
    /**
     * 3.0.0 — the drag commit: fires ONCE per drag (pointerup) with the
     * node id and its final graph-space position. Persist it and feed it
     * back through `positions`.
     */
    onMoveNode?: (id: string, position: {
        x: number;
        y: number;
    }) => void;
    /**
     * 3.0.0 — the right-click tether commit: source → target. The
     * consumer mints the GraphEdge id and appends it to its persisted
     * links array.
     */
    onLinkNodes?: (fromId: string, toId: string) => void;
    /**
     * 3.6.0 — Delete/Backspace on the selected edge (typing-target
     * guarded). The id is `parent:${childId}` for derived edges, or the
     * GraphEdge.id for explicit links — the consumer resolves the kind.
     */
    onUnlinkEdge?: (edgeId: string) => void;
    /**
     * 3.6.0 — the auto-arrange delegate (see KnowledgeGraphHandle).
     * Omit it and the handle's autoArrange is a no-op.
     */
    onAutoArrange?: () => void;
    /**
     * 3.6.0 — every view change (pan/zoom) reports here so the HUD can
     * render the live zoom readout.
     */
    onViewChange?: (view: GraphView) => void;
    /**
     * 3.0.0 — user-dragged positions, merged OVER the deterministic
     * layout (the persistence round-trip: onMoveNode writes here).
     */
    positions?: Record<string, {
        x: number;
        y: number;
    }>;
    /**
     * 3.6.0 — the EXPLICIT links (GraphEdge[]), rendered as bezier edges
     * alongside the parent-derived edges. (3.0.0-3.5.0 shipped the
     * shapeless {from, to} pair; the id-ed GraphEdge replaced it.)
     */
    links?: GraphEdge[];
    /**
     * 3.6.0 — the HUD search: nodes (and edges) whose labels do NOT
     * substring-match (case-insensitive) take data-dim="true". Empty or
     * whitespace = no search dimming.
     */
    searchQuery?: string;
    /**
     * 3.9.0 — THE LAYOUT ENGINE mode (default "free"): "free" keeps the
     * current behavior (the deterministic radial base + persisted drag
     * positions winning); "tree" runs the pure top-down tidy layout
     * (drag/nudge disabled — the layout is the law; pan/zoom/tether/add
     * still work); "radial" runs the ring engine with no drag overlay.
     * data-layout-mode rides the svg for probes.
     */
    layoutMode?: GraphLayoutMode;
    /** The svg's rendered height in px. Default 320. */
    height?: number;
    /** The accessible name for the graph application. Default "Knowledge graph". */
    label?: string;
    /** Renders the compact add-and-link toolbar. Default false. */
    addOn?: boolean;
}
```

#### smoothPath() (smoothPath)

Copy-paste JSX:

```tsx
import { smoothPath } from "@edwyn/signature-style/react";

// Catmull-Rom → bezier path string for N points { x, y } — the same
// smoothing AreaChart draws with, exported pure for your own SVGs.
const d = smoothPath([
  { x: 0, y: 180 }, { x: 60, y: 140 }, { x: 120, y: 90 }, { x: 180, y: 30 },
]);
// → "M 0 180 C …" (a ready-to-wear <path d={d} />)
```

#### layoutGraph() (layoutGraph)

Copy-paste JSX:

```tsx
import { layoutGraph, type GraphNode } from "@edwyn/signature-style/react";

// Deterministic radial layout: roots centered, BFS depth rings at
// radius 90 + depth·110, children fanned around the parent's angle,
// ties broken by id hash. Same nodes → same coordinates, always.
const nodes: GraphNode[] = [
  { id: "root", label: "Core Engine", categoryToken: "--sig-lavender" },
  { id: "venue", label: "Venue", parentId: "root", categoryToken: "--sig-mauve-soft" },
];
const positions: Record<string, GraphPosition> = layoutGraph(nodes);
```

#### cubicBezierEdge() (cubicBezierEdge)

Copy-paste JSX:

```tsx
import { cubicBezierEdge } from "@edwyn/signature-style/react";

// One cubic-Bezier edge path per node-with-parent — control points
// 60% along the radial. Feed it the layoutGraph output.
const d = cubicBezierEdge(
  { x: 320, y: 160 },
  { x: 210, y: 80 },
);
// → a ready-to-wear <path d={d} /> connecting parent → child
```

export interface DataTableProps {

Props surface — react/editorial.d.ts (`CarouselProps`):

```ts
export interface CarouselProps {
    /** The accessible name for the scroll region (role="region"). */
    label?: string;
    /**
     * 3.0.0 — THE MODE; 3.6.0 rebuilds paged-3 as TRUE PAGE GRIDS.
     * "free-scroll" (default) is the historical snap strip: every child is
     * a content-width snap unit, Prev/Next advance ONE ITEM, dots are one
     * per child, and the active index syncs through an
     * IntersectionObserver (majority-visible item = active). "paged-3"
     * chunks the children into pages of THREE (pure math: ceil(n / 3))
     * and renders a STATEFUL PAGE DECK — one `.sig-carousel__page` grid
     * (repeat(3, minmax(0, 1fr)), 16px gap, stretch) visible at a time;
     * non-current page wrappers carry `hidden` + `inert` (the inert
     * sweep: off-screen pages leave both the a11y tree and the tab
     * order), dots are ONE PER PAGE, Prev/Next step pages and disable at
     * the bounds, the indicator reads "Page p of P", and ←/→ (focus
     * anywhere inside the carousel) flip pages.
     */
    mode?: "paged-3" | "free-scroll";
    /** The items — must already be `<CarouselItem>` elements. */
    children?: ReactNode;
}
```

     * banner: a release note is the house voice). Rendered INLINE as

     * Override the mood's default icon (info → "Info", warning →
     * "TriangleExclamationPoint", announcement → "Megaphone" — all
     * gate-probed against the LIVE lucide map; this future-major map
     * spells the warning triangle "TriangleExclamationPoint", not
     * "TriangleAlert", the "Music" lesson again). Must be a real
     * lucide key — the IconName contract makes a typo a compile error.
     */

    action?: AnnouncementBannerAction;
    /** Renders the ghost close button (aria-label "Dismiss"). */
    dismissible?: boolean;

#### ToastProvider (ToastProvider)

```tsx

```

#### useToast() (useToast)

Copy-paste JSX:

```tsx
import { useToast } from "@edwyn/signature-style/react";

// inside <AttendanceForm>, beneath the provider:
const toast = useToast();
toast("success", "Attendance saved — see you there 🎉");
```

Props surface — react/toast.d.ts (`ToastFn`):

```ts
export type ToastFn = (status: ToastStatus, message: string) => void;
/**
 * `<ToastProvider>` — mounts the toast region on document.body and hands
 * `toast(status, message)` to the tree via context.
 *
 * Wrap an app once; call `useToast()` anywhere beneath it. The region is
 * role="status" aria-live="polite", fixed bottom-right at the zenith
 * z-rung (css/toast.css). Zero dependencies beyond react/react-dom.
 *
 * @example
 * ```tsx
 * <ToastProvider>
 *   <AttendanceForm />
 * </ToastProvider>
 *
 * // inside <AttendanceForm>:
 * const toast = useToast();
 * toast("success", "Attendance saved");
 * toast("error", "Could not save — try again");
 * ```
 */
export declare function ToastProvider({ children }: {
    children?: ReactNode;
}): import("react").JSX.Element;
/**
 * `useToast()` — the push function: `toast(status, message)`.
 *
 * Requires a `<ToastProvider>` ancestor; throws a named error at call
 * time otherwise (fail loudly, not silently).
 *
 * @example
 * ```tsx
 * const toast = useToast();
 * <button
 *   className="btn-primary"
 *   onClick={() => toast("success", "Saved")}
 * >Save</button>
 * ```
 */
export declare function useToast(): ToastFn;
```

### Set 08 — Motion & Kinetics

The kinetic engine's own set: the linear() spring tokens, the three motion primitives and the two release patterns (time dilation, fallback-first data). These frames mount in the MOTION LAB view (#/motion) — the lab stages the live choreography, the Copy Cards carry the recipes.

#### The kinetic tokens (KineticTokens)

Copy-paste JSX:

```tsx
/* 3.7.0 — the Motion section of css/tokens.css (:root, theme-independent).
   Four NATIVE linear() spring curves (zero animation libraries) + four
   scale-derived durations + ONE time-dilation master dial.

   Browser support: linear() is Chrome 113+ / Safari 17.2 / Firefox 112+.
   tokens.css carries a @supports fallback re-declaring all four as
   cubic-bezier approximations (snappy 0.34,1.56,0.64,1 · gentle
   0.25,1.25,0.45,1 · kinetic-out 0.16,1,0.3,1 · glide 0.4,0,0.2,1). */

--ease-spring-snappy: linear(0, 0.44 6.4%, 0.83 12.9%, 1.02 18.6%, 1.08 24.2%,
  1.09 28.9%, 1.05 34.9%, 0.98 42.4%, 0.97 48.5%, 1.01 58.6%, 1 69.1%, 1);
--ease-spring-gentle: linear(0, 0.36 8.9%, 0.68 17.9%, 0.9 26.1%, 1.01 34.9%,
  1.06 44.4%, 1.05 55.4%, 0.99 69.1%, 1);
--ease-kinetic-out:   linear(0, 0.61 10.8%, 0.91 22.7%, 1.02 34.3%, 1.05 45.5%,
  1.01 61.4%, 1);
--ease-glide:         linear(0, 0.63 14.5%, 0.95 30.2%, 1.02 42.5%, 0.99 57.1%, 1);

--dur-spring-snappy: calc(var(--sig-motion-scale, 1) * 320ms);
--dur-spring-gentle: calc(var(--sig-motion-scale, 1) * 480ms);
--dur-kinetic-out:   calc(var(--sig-motion-scale, 1) * 380ms);
--dur-glide:         calc(var(--sig-motion-scale, 1) * 280ms);
--sig-motion-scale: 1; /* the dial — Slow-Mo sets 0.25 */

/* REDUCED-MOTION MERCY: under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce AND the
   [data-sig-motion="reduced"] root override, all four durations
   collapse to 1ms — every kinetic transition becomes instant. */
```

#### AnimatedNumber (AnimatedNumber)

Copy-paste JSX:

```tsx
import { AnimatedNumber } from "@edwyn/signature-style/react";

<AnimatedNumber value={1740} prefix="$" />
<AnimatedNumber value={63.4} suffix="%" decimals={1} />
<AnimatedNumber value={12} suffix=" km/h" duration={480} />

/* rAF roll from the previous value, spring-interpolated (easeOutQuint
   + a damped 2% overshoot peaking at 70%). One <span class=
   "sig-animated-number">, tabular-nums — digits never jitter. No
   aria-live: the interpolation is decorative; the final value lands. */
```

#### MotionReveal (MotionReveal)

Copy-paste JSX:

```tsx
import { MotionReveal } from "@edwyn/signature-style/react";

{cards.map((card, index) => (
  <MotionReveal
    key={card.id}
    variant="fade-up"   /* or "scale-in" | "clip-reveal" */
    staggerIndex={index} /* delay = calc(index × 45ms) */
  >
    <StatCard {...card} />
  </MotionReveal>
))}

/* IntersectionObserver once-entrance (disconnects after revealing).
   Replay = remount (bump a React key). Reduced motion and
   [data-sig-motion="reduced"] ancestors reveal instantly. */
```

#### KineticSurface (KineticSurface)

Copy-paste JSX:

```tsx
import { KineticSurface } from "@edwyn/signature-style/react";

<KineticSurface accentToken="--sig-cyan">
  <p>Move the cursor across me — the sheen tracks it.</p>
</KineticSurface>
<KineticSurface accentToken="--sig-violet-glow">…</KineticSurface>

/* onPointerMove writes --ptr-x / --ptr-y (pixel coords) through a
   rAF-throttled setter; css/motion.css paints a 240px radial-gradient
   sheen at those coords (::after), fading in on hover. The POSITION
   repaints — it never animates; opacity is the only transition. */
```

#### The time-dilation pattern (MotionLabTimeDilation)

Copy-paste JSX:

```tsx
/* Slow-Mo: one custom property dilates EVERY kinetic duration on the
   subtree — set --sig-motion-scale on any container (the Motion Lab's
   control bar sets it on its root; 0.25 = quarter speed, springs
   visibly overshoot). */

<section style={{ "--sig-motion-scale": 0.25 }}>
  <MotionReveal variant="fade-up">…</MotionReveal>
  <AnimatedNumber value={63} suffix="%" />
</section>

/* The preview mercy: data-sig-motion="reduced" on the same container
   collapses the four duration tokens to 1ms — every spring inside
   lands instantly (the OS-level prefers-reduced-motion is honored
   automatically by css/tokens.css). */
```

#### The fallback-first data pattern (FallbackFirstData)

Copy-paste JSX:

```tsx
/* LIVE DATA CHOREOGRAPHY, zero keys: render deterministic offline
   sample data FIRST (labeled as a sample — never fake "live"), fetch
   the real stream on mount, swap in on success, keep the fallback on
   failure. AbortController cleans up on unmount. */

const [data, setData] = useState(SAMPLE_SERIES); // deterministic, labeled
const [status, setStatus] = useState("fallback"); // fallback|loading|live|error

useEffect(() => {
  const controller = new AbortController();
  setStatus("loading");
  fetch(OPEN_METEO_URL, { signal: controller.signal })
    .then((res) => {
      if (!res.ok) throw new Error(String(res.status));
      return res.json();
    })
    .then((json) => {
      setData(toSeries(json));
      setStatus("live");
    })
    .catch((err) => {
      if (err.name !== "AbortError") setStatus("error"); // fallback retained
    });
  return () => controller.abort();
}, []);

/* Failure is quiet on the auto-mount run (the sample IS the state) and
   loud on manual refetches (a toast names the failure). */
```

#### AuroraBorderCard (AuroraBorderCard)

Copy-paste JSX:

```tsx
import { AuroraBorderCard } from "@edwyn/signature-style/react";

<AuroraBorderCard accentTokens={["--sig-cyan", "--sig-orchid", "--sig-mint", "--sig-cobalt"]} trigger="hover">
  <p>The beam spins on hover.</p>
</AuroraBorderCard>
<AuroraBorderCard trigger="always">
  <p>The beam never sleeps.</p>
</AuroraBorderCard>

/* css/motion.css REGISTERS the angle (CSS @property, syntax "<angle>"),
   so the keyframe rotation interpolates per frame; the ::before is a
   conic-gradient cycling the accent tokens, mask-composited to a 2px
   ring (the border-beam technique). NO box-shadow is animated — the
   e1 treaty's registered-custom-property clause. Engines without
   @property keep a static 4-color ring; reduced motion holds it. */
```

#### TiltSurface (TiltSurface)

Copy-paste JSX:

```tsx
import { TiltSurface } from "@edwyn/signature-style/react";

<TiltSurface tilt={6} accentToken="--sig-rose-glow">
  <p>Tilt with the cursor — the sheen rides along.</p>
</TiltSurface>

/* perspective(600px) rotateX/rotateY tracking the pointer, rAF-throttled
   (the KineticSurface --ptr-x/--ptr-y math extended with --tilt-x/
   --tilt-y). Reduced motion: the tilt pins flat, the opacity-only
   sheen stays. */
```

#### StatusBeacon (StatusBeacon)

Copy-paste JSX:

```tsx
import { StatusBeacon } from "@edwyn/signature-style/react";

<StatusBeacon status="live" colorToken="--sig-green" />
<StatusBeacon status="syncing" colorToken="--sig-azure" size={12} label="Stream syncing" />

/* One span (the dot); ::after scales 1 → 2.2 and fades — the classic
   ping, transform/opacity only (the e1 treaty). role="status" carries
   the accessible name. Reduced motion: a static dot. */
```

#### WaveformBars (WaveformBars)

Copy-paste JSX:

```tsx
import { WaveformBars } from "@edwyn/signature-style/react";

<WaveformBars bars={16} colorToken="--sig-mint" label="Stream level" />
<WaveformBars data={[0.2, 0.9, 0.4, 0.7]} active={false} />

/* N bars, per-bar animation-delay (calc(--bar-i × 90ms)) on the snappy
   spring — the diagonal dance. Heights from your data (normalized) or
   the deterministic golden-angle curve (0.3 + 0.7·|sin(i·2.399 + 1.2)| —
   same input, same bars, NO Math.random). Reduced motion: static bars. */
```

## Full-Page Layout Blueprints (3.8.0)

Three self-contained full-page templates — one default-export React page each (playground/templates/*.tsx), composed exclusively from @edwyn/signature-style/react exports + the kinetic primitives, carrying an embedded token-driven <style> block (zero hex, 8px grid, container queries, reduced-motion honored). The CLI scaffolds them: vite-react/next hosts get the React blueprint (Signature<Name>.tsx), html/fresh hosts get the per-template static HTML mirror. In the playground's Templates Studio (#/templates) each blueprint previews live inside the viewport emulator (Desktop/Tablet/Mobile), re-themes under the scoped data-sig-theme stage wrapper, and copies as full TSX.

The registry: playground/template-registry.ts — PAGE_TEMPLATES: Array<{ id, name, description, Component, source }>.

### Blueprint saas — SaaS Landing

The marketing page blueprint: release banner, staggered kinetic hero, sheen feature grid, live billing switcher over the TierCard row, FAQ and structured footer.

CLI one-liner:

```bash
npx @edwyn/signature-style init --template saas
```

The full standalone TSX source (mechanically derived from the shipped component — never hand-edit this payload, change the .tsx and regenerate):

```tsx

/**
 * SaasLandingTemplate — FULL-PAGE TEMPLATE 01 of 3 (3.8.0 "Full-Page
 * Layout Templates, Interactive Viewport Previewer & CLI Template
 * Expansion").
 *
 * THE SAAS LANDING BLUEPRINT — one self-contained default-export page
 * composed EXCLUSIVELY from @edwyn/signature-style exports + the v3.7.0
 * kinetic primitives. Block by block, top to bottom:
 *
 *   1. AnnouncementBanner  — the Flamingo release rail (release-badge
 *      copy + the action button), dismissible.
 *   2. Centered PageHero   — staggered MotionReveal entrance: the hero
 *      block (h1 + subcopy) lands, then the dual CTA row (primary +
 *      secondary Button) follows on the 45ms stagger wave.
 *   3. Feature grid        — 3 columns of KineticSurface cards
 *      (cursor-tracking sheen), each with a tinted icon well
 *      (color-mix 12% of a --sig token) + h3 + copy. Three container
 *      tiers under the SHARED `template-stage` name (3.9.0): >1024px
 *      3 columns, 640–1024px 2 columns, <640px one column.
 *   4. Billing switcher    — package Tabs (Monthly | Annual — Save
 *      20%) with the FLIP gliding indicator driving ONE billing
 *      state; a live AnimatedNumber price strip recomputes (annual =
 *      20% off, computed) above the 3-column TierCard row (Starter
 *      $19, Pro $49 featured elevation, Enterprise $199).
 *      THE STRING-CONTRACT NOTE: TierCard.price is typed `string`, so
 *      the animated roll lives in the section's live price strip; the
 *      TierCard price lines re-render with the current cycle's value.
 *   5. FAQ                 — three AccordionCard entries.
 *   6. Structured footer   — brand column + three nav columns + the
 *      fineprint rule.
 *
 * STANDALONE PURITY: the page mounts its OWN ToastProvider (CTA +
 * banner clicks push toasts without assuming the host app provides
 * one), carries its CSS in an embedded <style> block (token-driven —
 * zero hex, 8px grid, container queries so the studio's viewport
 * emulator reflows the page, and the inherited motion-token mercy
 * covers reduced motion), and uses zero external dependencies.
 */
import { useState } from "react";
import type { ReactNode } from "react";
import {
  AnimatedNumber,
  AnnouncementBanner,
  AccordionCard,
  Button,
  Icon,
  KineticSurface,
  MotionReveal,
  PageHero,
  Tabs,
  TierCard,
  ToastProvider,
  useToast,
} from "@edwyn/signature-style/react";

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
/* The template's own stylesheet — embedded for standalone purity.     */
/* Token-driven only (zero hex), 8px-grid spacing, container queries   */
/* answer the STAGE width (the studio emulator), and every transition  */
/* rides the motion tokens (the reduced-motion mercy collapses them).  */
/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
const SAAS_TEMPLATE_CSS = `

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
/* Data — domain-neutral sample content (the standalone-purity voice). */
/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */

type BillingCycle = "monthly" | "annual";

/** Monthly base prices — annual renders 20% off, computed. */
const TIER_PRICES = {
  starter: 19,
  pro: 49,
  enterprise: 199,
} as const;

/** Annual discount — the owner spec: "annual = 20% off computed". */
const ANNUAL_DISCOUNT = 0.8;

interface Feature {
  icon: "Layers" | "Boxes" | "BadgeCheck";
  title: string;
  copy: string;
  token: "--sig-lavender" | "--sig-cyan" | "--sig-mint";
}

const FEATURES: Feature[] = [
  {
    icon: "Layers",
    title: "Token Cascade",
    copy: "Every hover, focus and disabled state derives from the core tokens — no hand-authored hex anywhere on the page.",
    token: "--sig-lavender",
  },
  {
    icon: "Boxes",
    title: "Zero-dependency core",
    copy: "One CSS bundle and typed React primitives. No runtime, no build step, no vendor lock — copy-paste and ship.",
    token: "--sig-cyan",
  },
  {
    icon: "BadgeCheck",
    title: "WCAG-gated themes",
    copy: "Three verified surface themes with measured contrast per token — the light variant re-inks every accent.",
    token: "--sig-mint",
  },
];

interface Tier {
  key: keyof typeof TIER_PRICES;
  name: string;
  token: "--sig-sky" | "--sig-mauve-soft" | "--sig-peach";
  featured: boolean;
  features: string[];
}

const TIERS: Tier[] = [
  {
    key: "starter",
    name: "Starter",
    token: "--sig-sky",
    featured: false,
    features: ["One project", "Core component set", "Community support"],
  },
  {
    key: "pro",
    name: "Pro",
    token: "--sig-mauve-soft",
    featured: true,
    features: ["Unlimited projects", "All 26 content tokens", "Full-page templates", "Priority support"],
  },
  {
    key: "enterprise",
    name: "Enterprise",
    token: "--sig-peach",
    featured: false,
    features: ["Everything in Pro", "On-prem tokens.css", "Design review sessions", "Dedicated channel"],
  },
];

const FAQ_ENTRIES: Array<{ title: string; body: ReactNode }> = [
  {
    title: "Can I use the templates commercially?",
    body: (
      <p>
        Yes — the MIT license covers every template and the whole engine.

    ),
  },
];

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */

function ReleaseBanner(): ReactNode {
  const toast = useToast();
  return (
    <AnnouncementBanner
      variant="announcement"
      dismissible
      action={{
        label: "Read the release notes",
        onClick: () => toast("success", "The full changelog lives in the package README."),
      }}
    >
      <span data-testid="tpl-saas-banner">
        v1.0 — full-page templates are here: three blueprints, one CLI
        command each.
      </span>
    </AnnouncementBanner>
  );
}

function HeroBlock(): ReactNode {
  const toast = useToast();
  return (
    <header className="sig-tpl-saas__hero">
      <MotionReveal variant="fade-up" staggerIndex={0}>
        <PageHero
          title="Ship your signature"
          subtitle="one import · three themes · zero dependencies"

            variant="primary"

            Start building
          </Button>

            variant="secondary"
